span.label: Formal logic does not supply the meanings it appears to encode: knowing what the predicates mean requires already knowing which individuals fall into the classes they name.
span.note: what this limits: a legal rule encoded in predicate logic as a representation of its meaning: the paper states one must already assume knowledge of which individuals have the properties named by the predicates
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reasoning the systems are meant to support is stated to be unmechanisable.
span.note: what this limits: a legal expert system as a substitute for legal reasoning: the paper states much of the required reasoning needs creative thinking, judgment and accountability, and cannot be mechanised
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper relabels the systems to scope the claim, while explicitly not denying their value.
span.note: what this limits: the label 'expert system' for these tools: the paper proposes 'bureaucratic expert systems' as the accurate description, while stating this does not deny their potential value
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's central objection is put as a question about TRANSFER rather than as a demonstration: why expect a logic devised by mathematicians for their own work to move comfortably into law and other practical social affairs, which do not share its special properties. The argument is that the transfer was never licensed, not that a particular system was measured and failed.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Weber's ideal-type model of bureaucratic administration is applied to rule-based legal expert systems, which is what licenses the paper's reclassification of them as 'bureaucratic' rather than 'legal' expert systems

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER RENAMES ITS TARGET IN ORDER TO SCOPE ITS OWN CRITIQUE, and says exactly what the rename does: systems that cannot handle interpretation 'do not deserve the epithet EXPERT. At best they can be called BUREAUCRATIC EXPERT SYSTEMS, which is NOT TO DENY THEIR POTENTIAL VALUE, only to recognise honestly their limitations.' The relabelling is the argument - move the name and the claim becomes true of a narrower thing.

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE MECHANISM BY WHICH A FORMALISM APPEARS TO CARRY MEANING IT DOES NOT: symbols 'that look like natural language', invested with meaning by the analyst, so a reader 'may imagine - as an unscrupulous expert system vendor may intend - that the computer understands the meanings of the natural language words'. The resemblance to English is doing work the logic is not.

span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE MEANING IS SHARED OR PRIVATE: each application invents its own language, which blocks data exchange AND makes it 'impossible to integrate legal expert systems by the obvious, simple method of merging rules'. A formalism that cannot be merged with another formalism of the same kind · strength of the relation: 0.8

span.label: A legal expert system built on propositional logic has essentially no semantics of its own: whoever assigns truth-values to the elementary propositions performs all the interpretation, and the machine merely computes consequences.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Propositional logic cannot represent any unit smaller than a whole proposition, so the word-level meanings that lawyers argue about cannot be encoded in it at all.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Predicate logic leaves the ontology to the analyst's discretion — the same content can be modelled either as a separate individual or folded into a longer predicate — so what exists in the knowledge base is decided arbitrarily.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two knowledge engineers formalizing the same legal concept in predicate logic will arrive at the identical expression only by chance, because paraphrases of the same rule need share no common term.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because each application invents its own private predicate language, separate legal knowledge bases cannot be integrated by simply merging their rules.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Truth-functional semantics fails for law because in a dispute truth is the negotiated endpoint of the process rather than a fact available at the start.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the proposed framework, existence here-and-now replaces truth as the primitive concept, on the grounds that existence can be operationalised whereas truth in social behaviour presupposes agents reaching consensus.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because every realisation in Norma carries an authority, the formalism always points back to the human agents in the social system who are responsible for its constructs.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Norma cannot be treated as a closed formal system: every behaviour it represents drags in further associated behaviours (ability, beginning, ending, sign, authority) recursively, so an open system is the only possible representation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The MEASUR method of analysis, developed from large numbers of legal and business cases, yielded systems cheaper to build and far cheaper to maintain than those built with conventional methodologies.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
